items.headline: Trump Administration Appeals CIT Refund Order for Finally Liquidated Entries
items.summary: The government filed an appeal challenging the CIT's authority to issue universal injunctions for finally liquidated entries where importers haven't filed suit. The appeal specifically targets entries already 'finally liquidated' for importers without CIT cases. CBP continues processing $85B in refunds for unliquidated entries through CAPE.

items.headline: CAPE Processing Milestone: 157K Declarations, $20.6B Already Processed
items.summary: CBP reports 157,402 CAPE declarations submitted with 70% passing validation. Approximately 15.9 million entries validated, $85 billion in claims accepted, and $20.6 billion already processed through refund component. Claims showing status shift from 'accepted' to 'updated' indicating active processing.

items.headline: 126K CAPE Declarations Filed, $35.5B in Anticipated Refunds Processed
items.summary: CBP filed updated progress report showing 126,237 CAPE declarations submitted since April 20 launch. Over 15 million entries accepted for IEEPA duty removal, with 8.3 million entries liquidated/reliquidated. Anticipated refund amount of $35.46 billion (principal plus interest) for processed entries.

items.headline: CAPE Phase 1 Goes Live - Refund Portal Now Accepting Claims
items.summary: CBP launched CAPE Phase 1 at 8am EDT allowing importers to submit refund claims for unliquidated entries and those within 80 days of liquidation. System processes up to 9,999 entries per CSV declaration with anticipated 60-90 day refund timeline. Excludes reconciliation, drawback, and AD/CVD entries for future phases.

items.headline: CBP Commissioner Ordered to Court Appearance on CAPE Compliance
items.summary: Judge Eaton ordered CBP Commissioner Scott to appear in court June 9 to explain slow compliance in developing CAPE Phases 2+ for more complex entry scenarios. Court issued show cause order questioning why suspension of universal refund mandate shouldn't be lifted for finally liquidated entries.

items.headline: Section 122 Replacement Tariff Set to Expire - No Extension in Sight
items.summary: The 10% Section 122 global tariff expires automatically after 150 days unless Congress acts to extend. No extension bill has cleared committee, and President cannot extend unilaterally. USTR running accelerated Section 301 investigations on 16 economies as potential replacement mechanism.
